reviews.counterevidence: Jer.5.10-Jer.5.19: Cutting at 5:13 would separate the denied prophetic word from its fire-and-wood vindication.

challenges.counterevidence: Jer.33.14-Jer.33.26: Keeping 33:14-26 wholly indivisible is plausible; this child ends before the day-night covenant argument and requires collection hydration. / Independent retrieval could overstate a seam inside 33:14-26; this argumentative child must hydrate both neighboring oracle movements. / Detaching this child from 33:14-22 would conceal that it answers resistance to the same David-and-Levi promise cluster.

reviews.support: Jer.34.1-Jer.34.7: A Babylonian-allies siege synchronism introduces a direct go-speak commission announcing capture yet a peaceful death and royal funeral lament, while only two fortified cities remain.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.34.1-Jer.34.7: Joining the liberty covenant at 34:8 would merge a personal royal fate oracle with a later citywide social action.

reviews.support: Jer.34.8-Jer.34.22: A dated word follows Zedekiah's liberty covenant; officials and people release Hebrew slaves, then turn and re-enslave them. A word-event recalls the exodus release law, contrasts recent obedience with profaning reversal, and punishes covenant-calf participants by sword, famine, carcass exposure, and renewed siege.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.34.8-Jer.34.22: Absorbing the judgment speech at 34:12 would erase the narratively complete action-reversal that triggers it. / A cut before 34:18 would separate the liberty wordplay from the covenant-cutting sanction that specifies its consequence.

challenges.claim: The release performance and re-enslavement complete an action reversal at 34:11, after which a new word-event at 34:12 recalls exodus law and interprets covenant-cutting sanctions through 34:22.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Use Jer.34.8-34.11 as narrative trigger and Jer.34.12-34.22 as covenant-lawsuit response, requiring both beneath Jer.34.8-34.22; a unified surface must preserve the 34:12 disclosure reset and calf-rite consequence.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.34.8-Jer.34.22: Absorbing the judgment speech at 34:12 would erase the narratively complete action-reversal that triggers it. / A cut before 34:18 would separate the liberty wordplay from the covenant-cutting sanction that specifies its consequence.

reviews.support: Jer.35.1-Jer.35.19: A Jehoiakim-date command gathers the Rechabites in a temple chamber, Jeremiah offers wine, their refusal cites ancestral instructions, and the obedience contrast yields Judah's judgment and Jonadab's standing promise.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.35.1-Jer.35.19: Splits after 35:5 or 35:11 were rejected because command, refusal-performance, family rationale, national comparison, and concluding blessing are one test-sign sequence.

reviews.support: Jer.36.1-Jer.36.8: A fourth-year writing command seeks repentance; Jeremiah dictates all words to Baruch and, being restricted, commissions him to read the scroll on a fast day.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.36.1-Jer.36.8: Ending at 36:4 would detach scroll production from the first public performance for which it was made.

reviews.support: Jer.36.9-Jer.36.26: A ninth-month fast locates Baruch's temple reading; Micaiah reports it, officials summon and hear the scroll, react fearfully, question dictation, and instruct concealment. Officials deposit the scroll and report to the king; Jehudi reads successive columns, the king cuts and burns them despite protest, then orders the hidden writers seized.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.36.9-Jer.36.26: Cutting at 36:13 would separate public reading and report from the official hearing that the report immediately initiates. / Ending before 36:24-26 would omit the court's contrasting reactions and coercive consequence of the burning.

challenges.claim: Verse 36:20 relocates the scroll from the officials' chamber to the king's winter house and begins a new royal audience: Jehudi reads, Jehoiakim cuts the columns, and the fire consumes them. Treating 36:9-26 as one scene obscures the completed temple-and-official inquiry at 36:19.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Segment Jer.36.9-Jer.36.19 as the temple reading and official inquiry and Jer.36.20-Jer.36.26 as the royal reading, burning, and arrest order; hydrate both beneath the existing Jer.36.9-Jer.36.26 scroll-escalation parent.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.36.9-Jer.36.26: Cutting at 36:13 would separate public reading and report from the official hearing that the report immediately initiates. / Ending before 36:24-26 would omit the court's contrasting reactions and coercive consequence of the burning.

reviews.support: Jer.36.27-Jer.36.32: After the burning, a new word orders another scroll, dictates a Jehoiakim judgment, and narrates Baruch's replacement copy with many added words.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.36.27-Jer.36.32: Separating 36:32 would leave the replacement command and royal sentence without their performed textual outcome.

reviews.support: Jer.37.1-Jer.37.10: Zedekiah's accession and non-heeding frame an envoy prayer request during temporary Chaldean withdrawal; Jeremiah answers that Pharaoh will retreat and the besiegers return and burn the city.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.37.1-Jer.37.10: A seam after 37:5 would isolate the tactical pause from the oracle explicitly correcting its interpretation.

reviews.support: Jer.37.11-Jer.37.21: During the army's withdrawal Jeremiah leaves for Benjamin, is accused of desertion at the gate, denies it, and is seized, beaten, and imprisoned by officials. After dungeon confinement, the king secretly asks for a word; Jeremiah gives the Babylon verdict, challenges the false prophets, petitions against return, and is transferred with bread provision.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.37.11-Jer.37.21: Joining the king's prison interview at 37:16 would merge arrest causation with a later secret consultation after many days. / Ending at 37:17 would omit the prophet's counterquestion and the concrete custodial resolution of the audience.

challenges.claim: The notice that Jeremiah remained in the dungeon many days at 37:16 marks elapsed time and a scene change from gate arrest and beating to Zedekiah's secret consultation. The private word, counterquestion, custody petition, transfer, and bread allowance form a separate royal-interview resolution.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Expose Jer.37.11-Jer.37.15 and Jer.37.16-Jer.37.21 as two ordered children, with mandatory sibling hydration under Jer.37.11-Jer.37.21 so arrest causation remains connected to the later audience.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.37.11-Jer.37.21: Joining the king's prison interview at 37:16 would merge arrest causation with a later secret consultation after many days. / Ending at 37:17 would omit the prophet's counterquestion and the concrete custodial resolution of the audience.

reviews.support: Jer.38.1-Jer.38.13: Named officials hear Jeremiah's surrender-life proclamation, accuse him of weakening soldiers, obtain royal acquiescence, and lower him into a muddy cistern. Ebedmelech hears of the cistern, leaves the gate court, petitions the king, receives thirty men, supplies padded ropes, and raises Jeremiah to guarded custody.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.38.1-Jer.38.13: Combining Ebedmelech's rescue at 38:7 would obscure the completed hostile action before its reversal begins. / Extending into the secret consultation would conflate the rescue's physical completion with a new royal-prophetic encounter.

challenges.claim: Ebedmelech hears what happened at 38:7 and becomes the new acting subject, leaving the gate court to petition the king before reversing the completed lowering into mud. His rescue commission, padded-rope procedure, and lifting action constitute a second scene rather than merely the tail of the officials' accusation.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Represent Jer.38.1-Jer.38.6 as accusation and cistern confinement and Jer.38.7-Jer.38.13 as Ebedmelech's intervention and rescue, returning both with a Jer.38.1-Jer.38.13 episode parent.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.38.1-Jer.38.13: Combining Ebedmelech's rescue at 38:7 would obscure the completed hostile action before its reversal begins. / Extending into the secret consultation would conflate the rescue's physical completion with a new royal-prophetic encounter.

reviews.support: Jer.38.14-Jer.38.28: The king summons Jeremiah at a temple entrance, extracts truthful counsel, debates surrender, hears safety and city outcomes, imposes secrecy, and the officials' inquiry verifies their cover story through siege day.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.38.14-Jer.38.28: Cuts at 38:23 or 38:26 were rejected because decision counsel, confidentiality command, and successful concealment resolve the same consultation.

reviews.support: Jer.39.1-Jer.39.10: Siege dates culminate in a breach, Babylonian officials occupy the middle gate, Zedekiah flees and is captured and judged, while city destruction, deportation, and poor-land grants summarize the fall.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.39.1-Jer.39.10: A seam after 39:7 would separate the king's fate from the city's parallel collapse and population disposition.

reviews.support: Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14: Nebuchadnezzar commands Nebuzaradan to protect Jeremiah; named officials implement the order by removing him from the guard court and entrusting him to Gedaliah.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.39.11-Jer.39.14: Harmonizing this directly with 40:1-6 would erase the received text's second release setting; both scenes remain distinct but relationally hydrated.

reviews.support: Jer.39.15-Jer.39.18: A retrospective guard-court word commissions a personal message: city judgment will occur, but Ebedmelech will escape because he trusted.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.39.15-Jer.39.18: Attaching this to his rescue action at 38:7-13 would violate the received placement and obscure its own word-event frame.

reviews.support: Jer.40.1-Jer.40.6: A new word heading locates Jeremiah bound among deportees at Ramah; the captain interprets the disaster, frees him, offers Babylon or Judah, and Jeremiah chooses Gedaliah at Mizpah.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.40.1-Jer.40.6: Collapsing this with 39:11-14 would suppress distinct location, captor speech, and choice details rather than resolve their relationship.

reviews.support: Jer.40.7-Jer.40.12: Scattered field commanders hear of Gedaliah's appointment, gather at Mizpah, receive serve-the-Chaldeans and harvest counsel, and returning Judeans collect abundant produce.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.40.7-Jer.40.12: Ending after 40:10 would omit the diaspora-remnant response that demonstrates the governor's settlement policy.

reviews.support: Jer.40.13-Jer.40.16: Johanan and commanders warn Gedaliah about Ishmael and a foreign royal sponsor; Gedaliah disbelieves, then secretly rejects Johanan's proposed preventive killing.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.40.13-Jer.40.16: Joining the feast assassination at 41:1 would eliminate the suspenseful warning-and-refusal scene that makes the attack intelligible.

reviews.support: Jer.41.1-Jer.41.10: A seventh-month royal-lineage visit becomes the meal-table killing of Gedaliah and troops; eighty mourners arrive, most are slain at the cistern, and Ishmael carries captives toward Ammon.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.41.1-Jer.41.10: A break at 41:3 would detach the assassination from the subsequent concealment, massacre, and captive-taking in the same coup.

reviews.support: Jer.41.11-Jer.41.18: Johanan hears of the crimes, pursues to Gibeon's waters, the captives turn back gladly, and Ishmael escapes with eight men. Johanan gathers rescued soldiers, women, children, and court officers, camps near Bethlehem en route to Egypt, and the narrator gives fear of Babylon as motive.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.41.11-Jer.41.18: Including 41:16-18 would move from rescue action into the survivors' strategic encampment and fear-driven migration plan. / Absorbing the prayer request at 42:1 would blur the completed travel decision with a formally assembled prophetic inquiry.

challenges.claim: Ishmael's escape with eight men closes the Gibeon pursuit at 41:15. Verse 41:16 then recapitulates the people Johanan recovered before moving to a Bethlehem-area encampment and an Egyptward strategy motivated by fear of Babylon, so rescue action has yielded to migration planning.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Surface Jer.41.11-Jer.41.15 as pursuit and captive recovery and Jer.41.16-Jer.41.18 as remnant regrouping and flight transition; hydrate the ordered siblings through their Jer.41.11-Jer.41.18 narrative parent.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.41.11-Jer.41.18: Including 41:16-18 would move from rescue action into the survivors' strategic encampment and fear-driven migration plan. / Absorbing the prayer request at 42:1 would blur the completed travel decision with a formally assembled prophetic inquiry.

reviews.support: Jer.42.1-Jer.42.6: All commanders and people ask Jeremiah to pray and disclose their path; he agrees to report fully, and they invoke a true witness while pledging obedience whether pleasant or unpleasant.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.42.1-Jer.42.6: Joining the ten-day answer at 42:7 would collapse the petition-oath turn into the later oracle it awaits.

reviews.support: Jer.42.7-Jer.42.22: After ten days Jeremiah summons the whole remnant and reports a two-path oracle: remain and be built and protected, or enter Egypt and meet the feared sword, famine, plague, and curse. Jeremiah directly names the remnant, declares that they deceived themselves when commissioning prayer, and restates their certain death in Egypt.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.42.7-Jer.42.22: A division at 42:12 would separate the positive route from the negative alternative whose contrast constitutes the requested guidance. / Folding this into 42:7-18 would weaken the shift from reported divine answer to the prophet's exposure of the petitioners' bad faith.

challenges.claim: The direct address to the remnant of Judah at 42:19 shifts from the reported stay-or-Egypt oracle to Jeremiah's prosecutorial application. Verses 20-22 look back on the commissioned prayer, accuse the hearers of self-deception, and restate the consequence, giving the passage a discrete indictment coda.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Use Jer.42.7-Jer.42.18 for the complete two-path divine answer and Jer.42.19-Jer.42.22 for the compliance indictment, while a Jer.42.7-Jer.42.22 parent preserves the answer-and-response sequence.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.42.7-Jer.42.22: A division at 42:12 would separate the positive route from the negative alternative whose contrast constitutes the requested guidance. / Folding this into 42:7-18 would weaken the shift from reported divine answer to the prophet's exposure of the petitioners' bad faith.

reviews.support: Jer.43.1-Jer.43.7: After Jeremiah finishes speaking, arrogant leaders accuse him and Baruch of deception, refuse the command, gather every remnant member including both scribes, and reach Tahpanhes.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.43.1-Jer.43.7: Stopping after the accusation at 43:3 would omit the collective disobedience and destination that enact it.

reviews.support: Jer.43.8-Jer.43.13: A Tahpanhes word commands large stones to be hidden before Judean witnesses; the Babylonian king's future throne, conquest, captivity, temple-burning, and pillar-breaking interpret the deposit.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.43.8-Jer.43.13: A seam after 43:9 would detach the buried-stones performance from the royal-canopy and conquest meaning assigned to it.

reviews.support: Jer.44.1-Jer.44.14: An all-Judeans-in-Egypt address recalls Jerusalem's devastation, rejected prophetic warnings, current incense persistence, forgotten ancestral evil, and announces near-total destruction without return.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.44.1-Jer.44.14: Cutting at 44:10 would separate the historical accusation from the therefore judgment that closes the lawsuit.

reviews.support: Jer.44.15-Jer.44.30: The large assembly knowingly answers Jeremiah, refuses obedience, credits former abundance to Queen-of-Heaven offerings, and has women assert household authorization for ritual cakes. Jeremiah answers the men and women by linking remembered incense to desolation, then reverses their vow logic: they may perform it, but the divine name and remnant in Egypt will cease except for few escapees. A this-is-the-sign declaration validates punishment in Egypt by promising Pharaoh Hophra's delivery to enemies as Zedekiah was delivered.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.44.15-Jer.44.30: Joining Jeremiah's rebuttal at 44:20 would obscure the opponents' complete evidentiary claim before it is answered. / Ending at 44:23 would give the historical rebuttal without the explicit oath-contest and survivor outcome. / Merging into 44:20-28 would hide the compact corroborating sign formula and named royal analogy.

challenges.claim: Three marked speech acts structure this disputation: the assembly answers Jeremiah at 44:15, Jeremiah turns to the men and women at 44:20, and the 'this shall be the sign' formula opens the Hophra oracle at 44:29. One surface hides the opponents' completed testimony, the prophetic rebuttal, and the corroborating royal sign as distinct forms.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Create hydrated children Jer.44.15-Jer.44.19 for the Queen-of-Heaven countertestimony, Jer.44.20-Jer.44.28 for the rebuttal and name-withdrawal oracle, and Jer.44.29-Jer.44.30 for the Pharaoh sign beneath Jer.44.15-Jer.44.30.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.44.15-Jer.44.30: Joining Jeremiah's rebuttal at 44:20 would obscure the opponents' complete evidentiary claim before it is answered. / Ending at 44:23 would give the historical rebuttal without the explicit oath-contest and survivor outcome. / Merging into 44:20-28 would hide the compact corroborating sign formula and named royal analogy.

reviews.support: Jer.45.1-Jer.45.5: A fourth-year scroll-writing setting quotes Baruch's added-sorrow complaint; the response announces universal uprooting, forbids seeking greatness, and grants life as spoil.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.45.1-Jer.45.5: Joining the nations superscription at 46:1 would combine a private scribe oracle with a new collection title.

reviews.support: Jer.46.1-Jer.46.12: A single heading explicitly identifies the word concerning the nations before the first Egypt-specific battle title begins. An Egypt, Pharaoh Neco, Euphrates, and fourth-year title introduces shield-and-horse mobilization that reverses into panic, northern defeat, divine vengeance, and internationally heard shame.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.46.1-Jer.46.12: Absorbing 46:2 would make the pan-national collection heading indistinguishable from the Carchemish oracle's own superscription; retrieval requires child hydration. / A seam at 46:6 or 46:10 would fragment the preparation-to-collapse reversal under the same Carchemish heading.

challenges.claim: Jer.46.1 supplies the pan-national superscription, the word concerning the nations, whereas 46:2 opens the first nation-specific oracle with 'Of Egypt' and a dated Carchemish title. Combining them risks narrowing the collection heading to Egypt even when relation metadata separately records its wider scope.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Represent Jer.46.1 as a non-naked collection heading and Jer.46.2-Jer.46.12 as the dated Egypt battle oracle, with mandatory heading-scope hydration across the Jer.46.1-Jer.51.64 collection and no source-order preference.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.46.1-Jer.46.12: Absorbing 46:2 would make the pan-national collection heading indistinguishable from the Carchemish oracle's own superscription; retrieval requires child hydration. / A seam at 46:6 or 46:10 would fragment the preparation-to-collapse reversal under the same Carchemish heading.

reviews.support: Jer.46.13-Jer.46.26: A new word title names Babylon's coming strike; Egyptian city alarms, fallen warriors, derided Pharaoh, migratory Daughter Egypt, cut forest, and enemy delivery sustain one invasion poem.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.46.13-Jer.46.26: Cutting at 46:19 or 46:24 would detach preparation and humiliation images from the named invader and final handover.

reviews.support: Jer.46.27-Jer.46.28: A direct fear-not address to Jacob and Israel promises distant rescue, quiet return, divine presence, nation-ending judgment, and measured correction.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.46.27-Jer.46.28: Including this in the Egypt invasion poem would bury the audience reversal and remnant-preserving reassurance.

reviews.support: Jer.47.1-Jer.47.7: A Pharaoh-before-Gaza heading introduces northern flood, fleeing fathers, ruined Philistine helpers, bald Gaza and cut Ashkelon, then a sword-rest dialogue answered by divine appointment.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.47.1-Jer.47.7: Splitting before 47:6 would detach the personified sword's lament and answer from the coastal destruction that evokes it.

reviews.support: Jer.48.1-Jer.48.10: The Moab heading launches woes and destruction notices for named towns, ascent-and-descent weeping, Chemosh exile, universal city loss, flight counsel, and a curse on slack execution.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.48.1-Jer.48.10: Ending at 48:6 would omit the trust-and-deity rationale and execution curse that complete this opening downfall movement.

reviews.support: Jer.48.11-Jer.48.17: Moab's settled wine and unchanged scent invite coming tilters, Chemosh shame, warrior-boasting reversal, near calamity, and roadside proclamation among named cities.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.48.11-Jer.48.17: A break at 48:13 would leave the wine-jar prediction without the lament and heralding response it generates.

challenges.claim: The lament summons at 48:14-17 continues through Dibon and Aroer's commanded reactions in 48:18-20: descend, stand by the road, announce Moab's shame, and howl beside Arnon. The explicit judgment-on-the-plain formula at 48:21 offers a stronger catalogue onset than the town-address change at 48:18.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Extend the wine-metaphor and public-lament child through Jer.48.20, then begin a Jer.48.21-Jer.48.28 toponym catalogue and flight-call child; return both beneath the broader Jer.48.11-Jer.48.28 movement.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.48.11-Jer.48.17: A break at 48:13 would leave the wine-jar prediction without the lament and heralding response it generates.

reviews.support: Jer.48.18-Jer.48.28: Moab's settled wine and unchanged scent invite coming tilters, Chemosh shame, warrior-boasting reversal, near calamity, and roadside proclamation among named cities. A judgment-has-come formula enumerates plateau towns, declares Moab's horn and arm broken for self-magnification, and orders inhabitants to abandon cities for cliff nests.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.48.18-Jer.48.28: A break at 48:13 would leave the wine-jar prediction without the lament and heralding response it generates. / Separating the city list at 48:25 would detach the catalogue from its interpretive pride charge and flight command.

challenges.claim: Beginning this unit at 48:18 bundles the closing public lament with a plateau-town judgment catalogue that announces itself only at 48:21. The Dibon-Aroer exchange answers the calamity and broken-staff cry from 48:16-17, while verses 21-24 switch to formal place-name enumeration.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Move Jer.48.18-Jer.48.20 into the preceding Jer.48.11-Jer.48.20 lament unit and narrow this child to Jer.48.21-Jer.48.28, retaining a mandatory Jer.48.11-Jer.48.28 parent for continuity.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.48.18-Jer.48.28: A break at 48:13 would leave the wine-jar prediction without the lament and heralding response it generates. / Separating the city list at 48:25 would detach the catalogue from its interpretive pride charge and flight command.

reviews.support: Jer.48.29-Jer.48.39: Repeated we-have-heard language catalogs Moab's pride; divine knowledge of empty boasts turns into lament over Kir Heres and Sibmah's severed vine, silenced joy, and universal mourning.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.48.29-Jer.48.39: A seam at 48:33 would separate the arrogance indictment from the vineyard-and-joy collapse through which it is mourned.

reviews.support: Jer.48.40-Jer.48.47: An eagle spreads over Moab, hearts become laboring women, escape routes collapse through fear-pit-snare, Sihon imagery consumes fugitives, and a formulaic captivity-restoration coda closes the judgment.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.48.40-Jer.48.47: Ending at 48:46 would omit the explicit latter-days reversal and end-of-judgment subscription.

reviews.support: Jer.49.1-Jer.49.6: An Ammonite heading and inheritance question accuse Milcom's occupation, announce Rabbah's alarm and reversal, deride valley-trusting backsliding daughter, and finish with restored fortunes.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.49.1-Jer.49.6: Joining Edom at 49:7 would cross an explicit nation heading and a complete restoration subscription.

reviews.support: Jer.49.7-Jer.49.22: The Edom heading questions Teman's wisdom, summons Dedan to flee, contrasts gleaners with total exposure, removes human and rocky confidence, invokes Sodom, and ends with lion and eagle attack images.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.49.7-Jer.49.22: Possible cuts at 49:11 or 49:16 remain internal developments under the same Edom address and sustained no-one-like-me challenge.

reviews.support: Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27: The Damascus heading names Hamath and Arpad's sea-like anxiety, fleeing Damascus and labor pain, lament over the city of praise, fallen youths, and fire on Ben Hadad's palaces.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.49.23-Jer.49.27: Absorbing Kedar at 49:28 would ignore a new royal-date heading and desert-people target.

reviews.support: Jer.49.28-Jer.49.33: A Nebuchadnezzar-struck Kedar/Hazor title commands attack, tent-and-flock plunder, terror, deep retreat, and concludes with Hazor as a perpetual jackal haunt.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.49.28-Jer.49.33: Dividing Kedar from Hazor would be precarious because the heading couples them and the attack command carries through the final desolation.

reviews.support: Jer.49.34-Jer.49.39: A Zedekiah-beginning word heading introduces the broken Elamite bow, four winds and dispersion, divine throne and royal destruction, then a latter-days fortune reversal.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.49.34-Jer.49.39: Joining the Babylon collection at 50:1 would cross a new two-chapter national heading after Elam's restoration coda.

reviews.support: Jer.50.1-Jer.50.10: A Babylon-and-Chaldeans superscription leads to international banner proclamation, northern desolator, joined Israel-Judah weeping return, lost-sheep confession, flight command, and northern coalition plunder.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.50.1-Jer.50.10: A seam at 50:3 or 50:5 would fragment fall announcement and covenant-seeking exiles within the collection's opening reversal.

reviews.support: Jer.50.11-Jer.50.20: Plundering rejoicers become a shamed wilderness mother; archers repay Babylon, Assyrian precedent explains northern-king punishment, and the scattered flock returns to pasture with pardoned remnant.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.50.11-Jer.50.20: Cutting at 50:16 would detach Babylon's repayment from the Israel-Assyria comparison and restoration that interpret it.

reviews.support: Jer.50.21-Jer.50.32: An attack command against named symbolic lands expands through hammer-breaking, divine snare, opened armory, extermination orders, and a repeated proud-one downfall with no raiser.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.50.21-Jer.50.32: A break at 50:28 would separate the temple-vengeance report from the pride-repayment commands that enact it.

reviews.support: Jer.50.33-Jer.50.40: Oppressed Israel and Judah receive a strong Redeemer who pleads their cause; sword formulas strike Babylonians, officials, diviners, warriors, resources, and treasures before Sodom-like desolation.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.50.33-Jer.50.40: Ending at 50:34 would isolate the legal assurance from the sword litany that states how the cause is prosecuted.

reviews.support: Jer.50.41-Jer.50.46: A northern host announcement makes Babylon's king labor in anguish, then reuses lion-from-Jordan and no-one-like-me imagery before the earth trembles at Babylon's capture.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.50.41-Jer.50.46: Combining chapter 51's wind decree would cross from this completed invading-army tableau to a fresh destroyer summons.

reviews.support: Jer.51.1-Jer.51.14: A destroying wind, winnowers, and armed attackers answer Babylon's guilt while Israel is declared not widowed; fugitives urge flight, recall attempted healing, and invite proclamation of Zion's vindication. Medes sharpen arrows for temple vengeance, banners and ambush enact the divine plan against wealthy Babylon, and a thunder-rain creation hymn contrasts the Maker with foolish idol-makers.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.51.1-Jer.51.14: A seam at 51:5 would divide the attack decree from the communal escape-and-testimony response it generates. / Splitting at 51:14 would detach the mobilization oath from the Creator's power confession that grounds it.

challenges.claim: Jer.51.11 resets the addressee with arrow-and-shield imperatives and names the kings of the Medes; temple vengeance, banner and ambush commands, and the oath at 51:14 then lead into the creator-idol hymn at 51:15-19. Ending at 51:14 bisects that mobilization-and-grounding movement and appends its first half to the destroying-wind testimony.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Repartition the material as Jer.51.1-Jer.51.10 and Jer.51.11-Jer.51.19, then hydrate those children with Jer.51.20-Jer.51.26 beneath a Jer.51.1-Jer.51.26 parent while preserving the received-order disclosure.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.51.1-Jer.51.14: A seam at 51:5 would divide the attack decree from the communal escape-and-testimony response it generates. / Splitting at 51:14 would detach the mobilization oath from the Creator's power confession that grounds it.

reviews.support: Jer.51.15-Jer.51.26: Medes sharpen arrows for temple vengeance, banners and ambush enact the divine plan against wealthy Babylon, and a thunder-rain creation hymn contrasts the Maker with foolish idol-makers. A repeated with-you litany names Babylon as the instrument smashing nations, armies, households, and governors, then turns against the destroying mountain and leaves it a burnt unusable ruin.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.51.15-Jer.51.26: Splitting at 51:14 would detach the mobilization oath from the Creator's power confession that grounds it. / Ending before 51:25 would leave the war-club catalogue without the reversal that judges the instrument itself.

challenges.claim: The anaphoric 'you are my war club' address at 51:20 opens a smashing litany after the creator-idol hymn closes with Jacob's portion at 51:19. Joining 51:15-26 suppresses that form and addressee reset, while starting at 51:15 also severs the hymn from the Medes-and-temple mobilization introduced at 51:11.
challenges.proposed_remedy: Close the middle child at Jer.51.19 after beginning it at Jer.51.11, and surface Jer.51.20-Jer.51.26 as the war-club and destroying-mountain oracle; hydrate both with the preceding Jer.51.1-Jer.51.10 child.
challenges.counterevidence: Jer.51.15-Jer.51.26: Splitting at 51:14 would detach the mobilization oath from the Creator's power confession that grounds it. / Ending before 51:25 would leave the war-club catalogue without the reversal that judges the instrument itself.

reviews.support: Jer.51.27-Jer.51.33: Banner, trumpet, nations, kingdoms, governors, horses, and warriors muster against Babylon; messengers announce captured crossings and burning reeds before Daughter Babylon becomes a ready threshing floor.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.51.27-Jer.51.33: A cut at 51:30 would separate the failed defenders from the relay report and threshing interpretation of their collapse.

reviews.support: Jer.51.34-Jer.51.40: Zion accuses Nebuchadnezzar of swallowing and emptying her; a divine plea-and-vengeance answer dries Babylon's sea, desolates the city, and turns roaring lions into a fatal perpetual feast.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.51.34-Jer.51.40: Splitting complaint from reply would destroy the direct wrong-remedy structure signaled by therefore at 51:36.

reviews.support: Jer.51.41-Jer.51.48: Captured Sheshach and sea-covered Babylon lead to ruined cities and Bel's disgorging; the remnant is told to flee without fearing yearly rumors while heaven and earth sing over northern destroyers.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.51.41-Jer.51.48: A seam at 51:44 would detach Bel's reversal from the escape exhortation and cosmic response that complete it.

reviews.support: Jer.51.49-Jer.51.58: Babylon must fall for Israel's slain; escaped survivors remember Jerusalem, voice sanctuary shame, hear the invading-days answer, and watch broad walls and gates fall as peoples labor for fire.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.51.49-Jer.51.58: Cutting at 51:53 or 51:56 would fragment the shame petition, divine response, and final fortification-collapse sentence.

reviews.support: Jer.51.59-Jer.51.64: A fourth-year journey setting commissions Seraiah with Jeremiah's written Babylon disasters; he must read, pray, bind the scroll to a stone, cast it into Euphrates, and interpret Babylon's sinking.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.51.59-Jer.51.64: Ending at 51:58 would omit the enacted scroll sign and the explicit end-of-Jeremiah-words subscription that closes the collection.

reviews.support: Jer.52.1-Jer.52.11: A regnal notice and evaluation begin the appendix; siege dates, famine, breach, flight, capture, sons' execution, blinding, and Babylonian imprisonment complete the king's downfall.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.52.1-Jer.52.11: Joining the temple destruction at 52:12 would merge the royal-fate scene with a new captain-led demolition episode dated separately.

reviews.support: Jer.52.12-Jer.52.16: A fifth-month captain arrival precedes temple, palace, and house burning, wall demolition, deportation, and the deliberate retention of poor vinedressers and farmers.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.52.12-Jer.52.16: Adding the bronze dismantling at 52:17 would shift from population and city action into an inventory-centered temple-plunder report.

reviews.support: Jer.52.17-Jer.52.23: Chaldeans dismantle pillars, bases, and sea, carry small utensils and precious metals, and the narrator measures columns, capitals, network, and pomegranates.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.52.17-Jer.52.23: A cut at 52:20 would detach the enumerated bronze weight from the architectural measurements that specify the plundered objects.

reviews.support: Jer.52.24-Jer.52.27: The captain takes named priestly, military, scribal, and citizen officials; the Babylonian king strikes them at Riblah, ending with Judah's exile formula.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.52.24-Jer.52.27: Combining the deportee totals at 52:28 would mix a narrated elite execution list with a separately dated numerical register.

reviews.support: Jer.52.28-Jer.52.30: Three regnal-year entries enumerate deportees in compact administrative style and conclude with an aggregate total.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.52.28-Jer.52.30: Attaching Jehoiachin's release at 52:31 would cross from tabular population accounting to a dated court-restoration vignette.

reviews.support: Jer.52.31-Jer.52.34: A thirty-seventh-year and twelfth-month date introduces Evilmerodach's accession favor: prison release, kind speech, elevated seat, changed garments, royal table, and lifelong allowance.
reviews.counterevidence: Jer.52.31-Jer.52.34: No further split was adopted because the elevation acts together form the appendix's final reversal scene.
